interpretation: The block-embedding arm delivered8/8 source requirements versus6/8 for structural grouping, but used12000 characters on every query versus3121.5 on average. This does not isolate a semantic-quality benefit from broader context.

Semantic groups were much coarser:35 versus175. It crossed heading boundaries20times and produced13 truncated parent excerpts across6queries. Heading changes/truncation counts are diagnostics, not automatic semantic-error labels.

The LLM produced one contract-valid Riks partition. Three other requests exceeded the5000output-token SDK limit, dominated by reasoning tokens. These are budget failures, not evidence that LLM boundaries are worse.
No subset-only LLM retrieval score, no structural fallback for missing LLM pages, no post-hoc increase of this batch budget, and no claim of a complete three-arm result.
